summary: A 1970 proposal to change the host-IMP specification to eliminate marking, by W. R. Crowther. It is a design suggestion for the interface between a host and its IMP.

plainLanguage.summary: This note proposes separating a message's leader from its text before sending them between a host and an IMP. The change is intended to make the text begin on a word boundary regardless of the machines' word lengths.

subtitle: A proposal to send the Host/IMP leader and message text separately to avoid marking problems.

tldr.problem: The Host/IMP specification packed the message leader and text together, causing marking problems across machines with different word lengths.
tldr.mechanism: The proposal separates the leader and text and sends them as consecutive messages in both directions.
tldr.outcome: BBN tentatively planned to implement the change alongside Host program changes and proposed giving one week's notice before a new release.

today: RFC 67 is an early proposal, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. The text says BBN tentatively planned implementation but does not report whether it occurred.

sections.title: The Marking Problem
sections.content:
W. Crowther reports a suggestion from Dave Walden: change the Host/IMP specifications to eliminate marking problems. The note says the packed leader and text caused the issue, but it does not define the marking problem in more detail.

The proposed goal is for message text to begin on a word boundary regardless of the word lengths used by the machines involved.
sections.plainLanguage: The note says packed message parts caused marking problems across machines. It aims to make the text start at a word boundary on every host.

sections.title: Separate the Leader from the Text
sections.content:
Instead of packing the leader and text in one message, send the leader and text as two consecutive messages. The text would then start on a word boundary.

The proposed change applies to both IMP-to-Host and Host-to-IMP messages.
sections.plainLanguage: Send the message information first and the text second. This separates the two parts in both directions.

sections.title: Tentative Implementation Plan
sections.content:
The authors see no disadvantages, and a sample of Host reactions ranges from neutral to very enthusiastic. BBN therefore tentatively plans to implement the change.

Because Host programs must also change, BBN proposes coordinating the new IMP release with those program changes and supplying updated Host specification text with one week's notice. It asks people to report objections quickly because a new IMP program version is already in progress.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN tentatively plans to make the change, but Host programs must change too. BBN proposes giving one week's notice before the new release.
